Two newer productions demonstrate Broadway's creative vitality. **Maybe Happy Ending** (85/100) earns acclaim as one of the most original musicals in recent years, telling an unexpectedly moving love story between robots that resonates with human emotion. Meanwhile, **Oh, Mary!** (84/100) offers something entirely different—Cole Escola's absurdist comedy reimagines Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed narcissist, delivering the kind of irreverent humor that has critics and audiences laughing in equal measure.

The top ten also includes enduring favorites like **The Book of Mormon**, **The Lion King**, and **Chicago**, proving that both satirical edge and spectacular stagecraft maintain their appeal. The timely revival of **Ragtime** adds historical weight to the season, while **Hadestown** and **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** showcase Broadway's commitment to theatrical innovation.

Whether you're drawn to groundbreaking new works or polished revivals, March 2026 offers exceptional options across genres and styles. Use the detailed reviews below to find the show that matches your theatrical taste.

best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back in March 2026 at the Broadway shows that opened in 2020—a year that would soon see theaters go dark for an unprecedented period—these five productions represent the last gasp of pre-pandemic theater, each capturing a distinct moment in Broadway's evolution.

Leading the pack is a reimagined **Les Misérables** at the newly refurbished Sondheim Theatre, where critics award this grittier reboot an 83/100, praising its fresh approach to the beloved musical even as some traditionalists remain skeptical of the changes. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** earns a 78/100 for its powerful Broadway debut, with Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama about racial tensions in a World War II Army base proving its examination of systemic racism remains urgently relevant decades after it was written.

The remaining shows illustrate the range of theatrical ambition in early 2020. Laura Linney commands the stage solo in **My Name is Lucy Barton**, an intimate adaptation that divides critics between those captivated by her luminous performance and those who find the theatrical framework lacking. **Grand Horizons** offers more conventional pleasures—a boulevard comedy about late-life divorce elevated by veteran performers Jane Alexander and James Cromwell. Meanwhile, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** proves the year's most polarizing production, with critics split between admiration for its bold vision and frustration with its departures from the classic.

With an average score of 74/100 across these five productions, the class of 2020 represents solid if not spectacular theatrical fare—a snapshot of Broadway experimenting with both reimagined classics and long-awaited premieres before everything changed.

With an average critic score of 81/100 across these ten productions, the 2021 Broadway season proves notable for its artistic ambition and diversity of voices. Whether you're drawn to intimate character studies, reimagined classics, or spectacular productions that have endured for decades, these shows offer something for every theatrical taste.

# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theatrical ambition cut short by unprecedented circumstances. These productions, many of which had brief initial runs before the pandemic shutdown, have earned their place in Broadway history through critical acclaim and artistic daring.

Leading our selection is **Les Misérables**, which scores highest with critics praising its grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, though the reimagined approach doesn't win over all traditionalists. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** stands as a watershed moment—Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally receiving its long-overdue Broadway premiere in a stellar revival that proves the work's examination of race and power within the military remains urgently relevant.

The remaining selections showcase Broadway's range during this period. **My Name is Lucy Barton** divides critics between those captivated by Laura Linney's luminous solo performance and those who find the adaptation too static for the stage. **Grand Horizons** offers boulevard comedy elevated by veteran performances from Jane Alexander and James Cromwell, even as some critics note its familiar territory. Rounding out the list, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining proves deeply polarizing—lauded by some for its bold vision and condemned by others for straying too far from the beloved original.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the class of 2020 demonstrates both artistic ambition and the enduring power of theatrical storytelling. Explore the full reviews and details to discover which of these productions might resonate with your theatrical tastes.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that premiered in 2021 represent a remarkable chapter in theater history—a season of reopening, reinvention, and artistic risk-taking following the pandemic shutdown. These productions, now five years into their runs or legacy, continue to shape conversations about what theater can be.

The ten highest-rated shows from that pivotal year average an impressive 81/100 from critics, reflecting a season of exceptional quality and ambition. Leading the pack is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance, which critics hail as mesmerizing and unforgettable despite—or perhaps because of—its experimental approach. Close behind, **The Phantom of the Opera** proves that Lloyd Webber's mega-musical spectacle remains potent even if campy, while **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** earns widespread acclaim for Rebecca Frecknall's immersive reimagining that transforms the entire Playhouse Theatre into a decadent nightclub.

The season showcased remarkable range: verbatim FBI transcripts (**Is This a Room**), solo virtuoso performances (**Lackawanna Blues**), epic financial dramas (**The Lehman Trilogy**), gender-swapped Sondheim (**Company**), and pop-concert reimaginings of Tudor history (**SIX**). What unites these diverse productions is their willingness to challenge conventions—whether through form, casting, staging, or subject matter.

Whether you're discovering these shows for the first time or revisiting productions that helped define Broadway's resilient return, this guide offers insight into the performances and productions that critics deemed most essential from that groundbreaking year.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands out as a remarkable year that brought both innovative new voices and powerful revivals to the stage. This collection of ten productions, averaging an impressive 83/100 critical score, showcases the breadth and vitality of American theater during a pivotal post-pandemic moment.

The season's crown jewel is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical about a teenager with a rare aging condition that critics consistently praise for its masterful balance of humor and heartbreak. Close behind are two landmark revivals: **Into the Woods**, a stripped-down reimagining that serves as a fitting tribute to Stephen Sondheim's legacy, and **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-musical that breaks new ground with its brazenly honest exploration of Black queer identity.

What distinguishes this collection is its concentration of Pulitzer Prize-winning works—five of the ten shows have earned theater's most prestigious honor, including Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog**, Tom Stoppard's deeply personal **Leopoldstadt**, and three contemporary American dramas exploring caregiving, trauma, and social inequality. The list also demonstrates Broadway's capacity for diverse storytelling, ranging from Mike Birbiglia's intimate solo performance about mortality to Jordan E. Cooper's audacious sketch-comedy satire **Ain't No Mo'**.

These productions represent a theater season that balanced commercial appeal with artistic ambition, featuring work from established masters and emerging voices alike. Whether you're revisiting these shows or discovering them for the first time, this guide offers a comprehensive look at the plays and musicals that defined Broadway in 2022.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As we look back from March 2026, the 2023 Broadway season stands as a remarkable period for dramatic theatre, yielding an exceptionally strong lineup that continues to resonate with audiences. The ten productions featured here maintain an impressive average critic score of 82/100, reflecting a year when serious drama flourished alongside innovative storytelling.

Leading the field is Maria Friedman's revelatory revival of **Merrily We Roll Along**, which finally gives Sondheim's notorious 1981 flop the production it always deserved. Critics praise its emotionally resonant approach, proving that sometimes a great work simply needs time and the right interpretation to find its audience. Close behind, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** demonstrates that theatrical adaptations of popular IP can transcend mere fan service when executed with technical brilliance and dramatic substance.

The season also showcased powerful ensemble work in **Appropriate**, Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama featuring Sarah Paulson, and the long-overdue revival of **Purlie Victorious**, Ossie Davis's 1961 satire that proves bracingly relevant more than six decades later. Meanwhile, **Parade**'s return offered urgent contemporary resonance, while **Stereophonic** captivated critics with its immersive three-hour journey into a 1970s recording studio.

What unifies these productions is their commitment to substantive storytelling—whether through classic revivals reimagined for contemporary audiences, bold new works tackling complex themes, or innovative adaptations that expand theatre's possibilities. For theatregoers seeking drama that challenges, moves, and lingers long after the curtain falls, these 2023 productions represent some of Broadway's finest recent achievements.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway enters spring 2026, the shows that debuted in 2024 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. This collection of ten productions—ranging from intimate character studies to lavish revivals—maintains an impressive average critic score of 83/100, reflecting a particularly strong theatrical season.

Leading the field is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's immersive rock drama set in a 1970s recording studio, which critics consistently describe as a theatrical marvel for its authentic depiction of the creative process. The show's meticulous attention to period detail and raw emotional honesty have made it a critical favorite, earning the highest score among 2024's Broadway offerings.

Close behind is **Operation Mincemeat**, a grassroots sensation that made the leap from fringe theater to the Great White Way. Critics praise its inventive ensemble work and infectious energy, proof that Broadway remains open to unconventional storytelling. Meanwhile, **Maybe Happy Ending** has charmed audiences and reviewers alike with its unexpectedly moving robot love story, earning recognition as one of the most original musicals to arrive on Broadway in recent years.

The diversity of this year's slate is notable: Cole Escola's absurdist farce **Oh, Mary!** offers riotous comedy, while Amy Herzog's **Mary Jane** provides understated dramatic depth. Traditional musical theater fans find satisfaction in lavish revivals like **Oliver!** and **Gypsy**, the latter featuring Audra McDonald's acclaimed interpretation of Mama Rose.

Whether you're drawn to experimental dance-musicals like **Illinoise**, historical narratives such as **Suffs**, or bold comedic reimaginings, the 2024 class of Broadway shows offers exceptional variety and quality worth exploring before their runs conclude.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays

As Broadway moves into March 2026, the plays that opened throughout 2025 continue to demonstrate the enduring power of dramatic storytelling on stage. This season showcases remarkable range—from bold revivals of American classics to inventive new works pushing theatrical boundaries.

Leading the field is Ivo van Hove's stripped-down production of **All My Sons**, which critics celebrate for its emotional rawness and ensemble excellence. The Dutch director's minimalist approach to Arthur Miller's family tragedy proves that sometimes less truly is more, allowing the text's moral weight to resonate with contemporary urgency.

Close behind, the 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** reminds audiences why this quirky musical became a phenomenon, with critics noting how its blend of humor and heart feels remarkably fresh two decades later. Meanwhile, **Paddington The Musical** captivates both families and critics with its technically stunning puppet work, proving that theatrical magic transcends age demographics.

The season's new plays also command attention. Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer Prize-winning **English** earns strong notices for its nuanced exploration of language and identity, while Branden Jacobs-Jenkins adds to his formidable body of work with **Purpose**, another incisive family drama. Feminist memory play **Liberation** generates discussion for its ambitious structure and timely themes, even as critics debate its execution.

With an average score of 84/100 across these ten productions, the plays from 2025 reflect a Broadway season willing to balance commercial appeal with artistic ambition. Whether you're drawn to reimagined classics, award-winning new voices, or innovative spectacle, this collection offers multiple entry points into the best of contemporary theater.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays: March 2026

As Broadway moves through March 2026, the year's new play offerings are beginning to take shape, with early productions setting the tone for what promises to be an evolving theatrical season.

The landscape for new plays this year launches with **Every Brilliant Thing**, which arrives on Broadway with a solid critical reception. The production earns a 76/100 score from early reviews, marking a respectable debut for 2026's play category. This one-person show, which explores themes of depression and resilience through an inventive list-making framework, brings an intimate theatrical experience to Broadway audiences seeking emotionally resonant storytelling.

With only one new play having opened so far this year, the 2026 season remains in its infancy. The average critical score of 76/100 suggests a competent start, though the limited sample size means the year's trajectory for serious drama remains largely unwritten. Historically, Broadway's play calendar builds momentum throughout the spring and fall, with March typically representing the tail end of winter productions before the pre-Tony Award rush begins in earnest.

The current theatrical moment reflects a cautious opening to the year, with producers and creative teams likely holding major productions for more strategic release windows. As we've seen in previous seasons, the concentration of acclaimed plays often clusters around award eligibility deadlines and high-traffic tourist periods.

For theatergoers planning their Broadway calendar, this early-year snapshot provides a starting point, though the coming months will likely bring additional productions that reshape the conversation around 2026's best plays.
